newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Far Eastern plans T$6 bln plant.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Far Eastern plans T$6 bln plant.

text.p: Taiwan's Far Eastern Textile said on Tuesday it plans to invest T$6 billion to build an integrated textile factory in the island's northern Kuanyin Industrial Zone.
"The plant will take a bit more than a year to finish, and it would feature one integrated production line," a spokeswoman for Far Eastern, who declined to be named, said by telephone.

She added the production line would have a daily capacity of 600 tonnes. The company planned to add two more production lines -- with daily production capacities of 400 tonnes and 200 tonnes respectively -- in later stages of construction.

"When the entire project is finished, Far Eastern would have a total daily integrated production capacity of 2,100 tonnes, making it the second biggest integrated textile producer in Taiwan," the spokeswoman said.
She identified Nan Ya Plastics as the biggest integrated textile producer.
Far Eastern declined to say when all the stages of construction for its new plant would be finished.
